title: Decision of the AI Office
summary: The Decision of the AI Office declares the office’s stance on a specific AI‑related issue, outlining the chosen course of action and its justification. It highlights key principles such as safety, transparency, and regulatory compliance that guide the office’s decisions.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Technology Specialists in AI
summary: This policy announces openings for technology specialists in AI, outlining the roles, responsibilities, and qualifications needed for the positions. It also sets forth hiring procedures and expectations for new hires in the AI department.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Lead Scientific Adviser
summary: The policy outlines the creation of a Lead Scientific Adviser position within the AI Office, specifying the role’s duties, required qualifications, and the appointment process. It emphasizes that the adviser will provide expert guidance on research, ethics, and policy decisions, ensuring scientific rigor and alignment with organizational goals.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Legal Officers
summary: The document explains how to fill open positions for legal officers working on AI matters. It sets out the hiring criteria, responsibilities, and application process for those roles.

title: AI Office Vacancy: Policy Officers
summary: The policy document announces a vacancy for a Policy Officer in the AI Office, outlining the role’s responsibilities, required qualifications, and application process. It emphasizes the importance of ensuring responsible AI deployment through oversight, compliance, and continuous policy evaluation.

title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts who evaluate and provide evidence‑based recommendations for the European Union’s proposed AI legislation. Their findings help lawmakers create rules that protect users while encouraging responsible AI innovation.

title: Draft Standardisation Request
summary: This document proposes a set of standardized guidelines for building and using AI systems, aiming to create uniform practices across the industry. It invites stakeholders to review and contribute feedback to shape clear, consistent rules that promote safety, transparency, and compliance with legal and ethical standards.

title: CoP Consultation Notice
summary: This notice announces a consultation about establishing or updating a Community of Practice (CoP) focused on AI policy and practice. It invites stakeholders to share feedback and help shape the CoP’s objectives, membership, and activities for better collaboration and governance.

title: CoP Call for Expression of Interest
summary: This document announces a call for individuals and organizations to express interest in forming or joining a Community of Practice on AI policy. It provides guidance on how to submit an expression of interest and explains the expected goals and benefits of participating.

title: CoP Graphic: Overview of Iterative Drafting Process
summary: This policy document gives an overview of the iterative drafting process used by the community of practice. It explains the stages of drafting, reviewing, and refining policy documents to ensure clarity, consistency, and stakeholder alignment.

title: CoP Graphic: Timeline of Drafting Process
summary: The document presents a visual timeline that tracks the drafting process of the CoP graphic. It highlights key milestones and dates that marked each stage of development.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This document presents a preliminary framework of guidelines and responsibilities for AI practitioners, emphasizing ethical standards and accountability. It serves as a starting point for stakeholders to review and refine best practices for responsible AI deployment.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The Code of Practice: 2nd Draft provides a framework of guidelines for organizations and individuals engaged in the creation, deployment, and use of AI technologies. It emphasizes principles such as transparency, fairness, accountability, and safety to help ensure responsible and ethical AI practices.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: This document presents the third draft of a Code of Practice for AI, outlining standards for ethical design, deployment, and governance. It offers guidelines for organizations to ensure responsible, transparent, and accountable use of AI systems.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft proposes an international agreement to coordinate the responsible and ethical development of artificial intelligence. It focuses on transparency, safety, and collaboration among governments, industry, and civil society to mitigate risks and maximize benefits.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final outlines the agreed‑upon principles and commitments that participating parties have reached regarding the development and deployment of artificial intelligence systems. It emphasizes transparency, safety, accountability, and equitable benefits, aiming to foster trust and cooperation across the global AI community.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: These guidelines list the AI practices that are disallowed, such as those that could harm people or infringe on privacy. They give a clear set of prohibited activities to help developers and users avoid unethical or unsafe AI use.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: The Guidelines on AI System Definition provide a framework for identifying and classifying AI systems, helping organizations determine which products and services fall under the definition of AI. The document outlines key criteria, responsibilities, and risk considerations that guide the development, deployment, and oversight of these systems.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This document outlines strategies for encouraging communication that supports the growth of start‑ups and fosters innovation. It highlights initiatives such as networking events, funding opportunities, and collaborative platforms designed to connect entrepreneurs with resources and stakeholders.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program that gives new technology companies in Europe access to high‑performance computing resources. By offering infrastructure, technical help, and possible funding, it helps start‑ups speed up AI and data‑intensive product development.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: The policy document is a slideshow prepared for a webinar that explains how to manage risks in AI projects. It covers the identification, assessment, and mitigation of potential risks to ensure safe and responsible AI development.

title: Video: Webinar on Risk Management
summary: This webinar video explains risk management, covering how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks in projects or business activities. It offers practical strategies, best practices, and real-world examples to help participants apply risk‑management techniques effectively.
